lines.text: Many learners say: You are a student?
A question starts with are, then you.
Are you! Are you a student?

data.why: A question starts with are, then you.

native.hook: 文末を上げるだけではダメ？
native.tip: 日本語は文末を上げると質問になりますが、英語は語順を入れ替えます。
native.caption: “You are a student?”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の感覚で、語順そのままで文末を上げてしまいがちです。“Are you a student?” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“Are you”。“Are you a student?” を声に出して言ってみよう。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: In Japanese, if you raise the end of a sentence, it becomes a question, but in English, you change the word order.
en.caption: Do you say this? “You are a student?” 😅 Do not only raise your voice. The natural way is “Are you a student?” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
